- state length: about 6 words each (one line: a subject, a chat message, a log line, a form field); every state within ±30% of that
- instruction length: very short (3-8 words)
- domain: logistics and shipping
- genres to spread across the sources: Slack/Teams thread, voicemail transcript, status update to a manager
- tone: bureaucratic
- instruction style for this batch: questions that first define the term ('A refund request means the sender explicitly asks for money back. Is there one here?')
- candidate-description style for this batch: one or two words per candidate
- names you may use (never reuse a name across sources): Leila Alvarez, Jonas Iyer, Jonas Kowalski, Leila Alvarez, Quentin Alvarez, Kwame Alvarez; companies: Kestrel Analytics, Bluefin Labs, Kestrel Analytics, Copperleaf Foods
- focus traps: distractor. Every question in this batch uses this trap (others may occur naturally).

- multilabel: at least one question in the batch has 3-5 correct candidates

Offer dated 4 April: Nadia Kowalski is being considered for the junior release-coordinator role. The stated base salary is $62,000 yearly. The hiring note says the candidate asked about compensation, but does not say she accepted the offer. This file is for recruiting review, not payroll.

Clause 6, original: “If the candidate signs by 18 April, Meridian will pay a $1,200 start bonus. No bonus is owed if the signed offer arrives after that date.” The clause separately offers $300 for each of the first four completed training modules, payable only after the candidate starts. These module payments are not part of base salary and are not the start bonus. A nearby budget row says the previous role had a $1,500 bonus; it is historical and does not amend this offer.

Amendment 1, dated 10 April: “Replace the signing deadline with 22 April. Bonus amount and all other conditions unchanged.”

Amendment 2, dated 15 April: “For this candidate only, signing deadline is 20 April, notwithstanding the 22 April date in Amendment 1. This amendment does not change the bonus amount.” Recruiter initials appear beside both amendments. A copied checklist elsewhere still says “sign by 18 April”; it was not revised and is not an amendment.

Receipt log: Nadia emailed the signed offer at 11:58 p.m. on 20 April, and the recruiting mailbox timestamp is also 20 April. Her email says, “I signed today; looking forward to talking through the training plan.” It does not claim she completed any modules or started work. The system converted neither timestamp into another date. A separate note says another candidate signed on 21 April, but that person is not Nadia. The offer has no weekend extension rule, grace period, or time-zone adjustment.

The four module names in the proposed training plan are Build, Test, Deploy, and Handoff. The coordinator’s estimate says completing all four would produce $1,200 in module payments (4 × $300). That amount happens to equal the start bonus, but the two payments have different conditions. An old spreadsheet total of $2,700 adds the historical $1,500 bonus to the proposed $1,200 module estimate; it is not Nadia’s approved compensation.
